sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: A form of government where the **executive** derives its democratic legitimacy from its ability to command the confidence of the **legislature** (Parliament) and is also held accountable to it.
Enshrined in the **Constitution of India**, which came into force on **26 January 1950**, drawing inspiration heavily from the **British Westminster Model**.
Where is it Located in Constitution?
Contained in **Part V** (Articles **79 to 122**) of the Indian Constitution, detailing the composition, officers, privileges, and powers of Parliament.
The Parliament of India consists of the **President**, the **Council of States (Rajya Sabha)**, and the **House of the People (Lok Sabha)**.
Why is it Important for UPSSSC PET?
Frequent questions appear on **article numbers**, **qualifications**, **money bills**, **joint sittings**, and **officers of Parliament** in competitive Uttar Pradesh exams.

• **Dual Executive** (Nominal and Real)
• **Majority Party Rule**
• **Collective Responsibility**
• **Political Homogeneity**
• **Double Membership** (Executive is part of Legislature)
Helps clear foundational concepts of Indian Polity tested in preliminary screening tests like UPSSSC PET with direct factual and article-based MCQs.
India opted for a parliamentary system rather than a presidential system due to its **social diversity**, **federal structure**, and the historical familiarity established during the **British Raj**.

items.title: Structure of Parliament & Mnemonic (SRL)
items.content:
• **Article 79** establishes the Parliament consisting of the **President**, **Rajya Sabha**, and **Lok Sabha**.
• **Rajya Sabha (Upper House)**: Maximum strength is **250**; represents the **states and Union Territories**.
• **Lok Sabha (Lower House)**: Maximum strength is **552**; represents the **people of India** directly.
• **Mnemonic for Articles (SIR)**: 
  - **S** = **S**arla (Article **79** = **S**ansad)
  - **R** = Rajya Sabha (Article **80**)
  - **L** = Lok Sabha (Article **81**)
• **Memory Trick**: **S**arla **R**oams **L**ondon (**S**ansad-79, **R**ajya Sabha-80, **L**ok Sabha-81).

items.title: Parliamentary Sessions & Mnemonic (BMS)
items.content:
• **Budget Session**: Usually from **February to May** (Longest session).
• **Monsoon Session**: Usually from **July to September**.
• **Winter Session**: Usually from **November to December** (Shortest session).
• **Constitutional Mandate**: Gap between two sessions must not exceed **6 months** (**Article 85**).
• **Mnemonic**: **B**ig **M**an **W**alks (**B**udget, **M**onsoon, **W**inter).

items.title: Types of Bills in Parliament
items.content:
• **Ordinary Bill**: Relates to any matter other than financial matters (**Articles 107 & 108**).
• **Money Bill**: Relates strictly to financial matters like taxation and borrowing (**Article 110**).
• **Financial Bill (I & II)**: Contains financial provisions along with other matters (**Articles 117(1) & 117(3)**).
• **Constitutional Amendment Bill**: Relates to amending the Constitution (**Article 368**).
• **Key Rule**: Ordinary bills require a **Joint Sitting** under **Article 108** if deadlocked, but Money Bills and Constitutional Amendment Bills **cannot** have a joint sitting.

items.title: Key Officers of Parliament
items.content:
• **Speaker of Lok Sabha**: Presides over Lok Sabha, decides **Money Bill** status (**Article 110(3)**), casts casting vote in case of a tie (**Article 100**).
• **Chairman of Rajya Sabha**: The **Vice-President of India** acts as the ex-officio Chairman (**Article 64** and **Article 89**).
• **Secretary-General**: Administrative head of each House secretariat appointed by the respective presiding officer.
• **Leader of the House / Opposition**: Crucial figures for managing legislative business and debates.

items.title: Parliamentary Committees
items.content:
• **Public Accounts Committee (PAC)**: Examines CAG report; has **22 members** (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha); Chairperson is always from the **opposition**.
• **Estimates Committee**: Largest committee with **30 members** (all from Lok Sabha); examines estimates included in the budget.
• **Committee on Public Undertakings**: Has **22 members** (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha) to examine reports of PSUs.

items.definition: Remember **79, 80, 81** using **S**arla **R**oams **L**ondon (**S**ansad = 79, **R**ajya Sabha = 80, **L**ok Sabha = 81).
Remember **Article 110** by associating '110 Volt Shock' with money matters as money bills are powerful and sensitive.
Remember **Article 108** by remembering 'Dial 108 for Emergency'—a deadlock in Parliament is an emergency requiring a joint sitting.
Remember **1/10th** (10%) quorum by matching the digit '10' in Article **10**0 (Voting and Quorum).
Remember Public Accounts Committee has **22 members** (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha). Math trick: **15 + 7 = 22**.
Remember Estimates Committee has **30 members** (all Lok Sabha, no Rajya Sabha members).

items.term: Mistake 1: Who presides over Joint Sitting?
items.definition: Students often think the **President** or **Vice-President** presides over a joint sitting. **Correction:** The **Speaker of Lok Sabha** presides over it (or Deputy Speaker in Speaker's absence).

items.term: Mistake 2: Is President a Member of Parliament?
items.definition: Students assume Parliament only means Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. **Correction:** Under **Article 79**, the **President** is an integral part of Parliament.
Students confuse Rajya Sabha with Lok Sabha regarding dissolution. **Correction:** Rajya Sabha is a **permanent house** and **not subject to dissolution**; only Lok Sabha dissolves.

items.term: Mistake 4: Who certifies a Money Bill?
items.definition: Students think the Finance Minister or President certifies a Money Bill. **Correction:** Only the **Speaker of Lok Sabha** has the final authority to certify a Money Bill.

items.term: Mistake 5: Rajya Sabha powers on Money Bill
items.definition: Students believe Rajya Sabha can reject or amend a Money Bill. **Correction:** Rajya Sabha can only delay a Money Bill for a maximum of **14 days** and give recommendations.

items.term: Mistake 6: Joint Sitting for Money/Constitutional Bills
items.definition: Students think a joint sitting can be called for all bills. **Correction:** Joint sittings are **never** held for Money Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills.
India follows a **Parliamentary System** modeled on the British **Westminster Model**, featuring executive accountability to the legislature.
Parliament comprises the **President**, **Rajya Sabha** (Upper House), and **Lok Sabha** (Lower House).
Maximum strength of **250** members, with **12 members nominated** by the President for specialized fields.
Maximum strength of **552** members, representing territorial constituencies across India through direct elections.
The constitutional gap between two consecutive parliamentary sessions must not exceed **6 months** (**Article 85**).
The minimum quorum to transact business in either House of Parliament is **one-tenth** (**1/10th**) of total members.
A Money Bill can originate **only in Lok Sabha** on the recommendation of the President and certified by the **Speaker**.
Resolved under **Article 108** for ordinary bills, summoned by the President and presided over by the **Lok Sabha Speaker**.
Includes **Public Accounts Committee (22 members)**, **Estimates Committee (30 members)**, and Public Undertakings Committee.
**Rajya Sabha** is permanent; one-third of its members retire every **2 years**, ensuring continuous legislative presence.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize the exact article numbers for Parliament (Articles 79, 80, 81), Money Bill (Article 110), and Joint Sitting (Article 108) as direct factual questions are frequently asked.
Examiners love asking who presides over a joint sitting of Parliament. Remember it is ALWAYS the Speaker of Lok Sabha, NOT the Vice-President or President.
Note that Rajya Sabha has NO power to vote on demands for grants; voting on demands for grants is the exclusive privilege of the Lok Sabha.

Do not confuse the maximum strength of Lok Sabha (552) with its current sanctioned or elected strength. Keep track of recent constitutional amendments regarding Anglo-Indian nomination removal (104th Amendment).

keyTakeaways: India's Parliamentary system is anchored in **Part V (Articles 79-122)** of the Constitution.
The Parliament consists of three units: **President, Rajya Sabha, and Lok Sabha**.
**Article 110** defines a Money Bill, which can only be introduced in Lok Sabha with prior presidential recommendation.
**Article 108** provides for a **Joint Sitting** of both houses, presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha.
The maximum gap allowed between two parliamentary sessions is **6 months** (**Article 85**).
Quorum for transaction of business in Parliament is **1/10th** of total members.
**Public Accounts Committee** has **22 members** and its chairperson is appointed from the opposition.
